questions.question: How do you write a function that adds two numbers?
options: def add(a, b): return a + b
function add(a, b) { return a + b; }
int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
#define add(a, b) ((a)+(b))
questions.explanation: function keyword, braces, return. No types on the parameters. No def, no #define.

questions.question: What is a function in JavaScript?
options: A value you can bind, pass, and return.
A statement that cannot be stored in a binding.
A C++-style nested function that must be declared inside main.
A type of number used only for callbacks.
questions.explanation: Functions are values. That is what makes closures and higher-order helpers possible.

questions.question: Lexical scope means which of these?
options: A function sees bindings from where it is written.
A function sees bindings from where it is called, like a dynamic scope.
A function sees only globals, never parameters.
A function copies all outer values at parse time and never sees updates.
questions.explanation: JS is lexically scoped. Closures still see live bindings, not snapshots.

questions.question: Why can you return an inner function that uses a local let without a dangling pointer?
options: Locals live on a C++-style stack and JS copies them into registers.
Bindings live as long as something still references them.
Inner functions are inlined, so no environment remains.
You cannot return inner functions; the engine throws.
questions.explanation: That is the heap-based model behind closures. C++ lambdas that capture stack by reference can dangle; JS locals do not.

questions.question: makeStatusMachine should hide status. Which design does that?
options: Put status on the returned object so tests can read machine.status.
Use a global let status so every machine shares one value.
Close over a let status and only expose get and set.
Store status in window.status for the debugger.
questions.explanation: A closed-over binding is not a public property. Callers cannot assign machine.status.

questions.question: Which are true of parameters?
options: They are local bindings for that call.
Extra arguments throw a TypeError by default.
Missing arguments are undefined unless you set a default.
They are always copied by value, including objects.
questions.explanation: Extra args are ignored. Objects are passed as references (the binding is local; the object is shared).

questions.question: function declarations vs const fn = function () {} hoist how?
options: Both can be called on the line above their source.
Only arrows are hoisted.
Neither can be called before the line.
Declarations are hoisted; the const binding is not initialized yet.
questions.explanation: A function declaration can be called earlier in the same scope. A const function lives in the temporal dead zone until its line.

questions.question: A closure keeps a live link. If the inner function reads a let that is later assigned, what happens?
options: It sees the new value on later calls.
It still sees the original snapshot from creation time.
The assignment throws because closed bindings are frozen.
It sees undefined after the outer function returns.
questions.explanation: YDKJS: live link, not a snapshot. Reassignment is visible.

questions.question: applyDiscount(0.1)(100) should be 90. Which shape is that?
options: A global rate variable set by applyDiscount.
A function that returns another function closing over rate.
A prototype method on Number.
A switch on rate inside a single function with two parameters only.
questions.explanation: The outer function captures rate. The inner multiplies amount.

questions.question: var vs let inside an if block inside a function: which leaks to the whole function?
options: let, because it is older than var.
both, because JS has no block scope.
var, because it is function-scoped.
neither, because if bodies are separate modules.
questions.explanation: let/const honor the block. var does not.

questions.question: makeIdFactory("inv")() then again should yield inv-1 then inv-2. Where does the counter live?
options: On the returned function as fn.n so callers can reset it.
In Math.random so ids are unique without state.
In localStorage so it survives refresh.
In a closed-over let, incremented on each call.
questions.explanation: A private counter is the point of the factory. Do not put n on the function unless you want it public.

questions.question: Which call is a closure in the observable sense?
options: A returned inner function that still reads an outer let after that call finished.
A function that only uses its own parameters and locals, called in the same scope it was defined.
Any function declared with function, even at global scope.
console.log, because it is built in.
questions.explanation: YDKJS: you observe closure when a function uses an outer binding from a scope that has already finished.

questions.question: set on a status machine should ignore undefined. Why?
options: undefined is the only falsy value status can have.
undefined means “no change” if a caller omitted the next status.
JSON cannot store strings, only undefined.
set must throw whenever the argument is not a boolean.
questions.explanation: Missing arguments arrive as undefined. Ignoring them keeps the last real status.
